newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- APRIL 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- APRIL 15.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The principle of "financing to achieve a target" in the development law, the option to sign collective agreements on a local level, restrictions on paid work for pensioners and reduction on non-wage costs for new employees are some of the major points the government will promote in social dialogue to begin soon between it, unions and employers. The 19-point document was sent to social partners yesterday, as a starting point for talks.

--The finance ministry yesterday said the operation of the economic crimes squad, SDOE, was completely within the law and that the issue currently under consideration at the Council of State - the country's highest administrative court - did not impinge on the SDOE's functions.

--The Capital Market Commission yesterday agreed with National Economy Secretary-General Apostolos Fotiadis that all those involved in working with or influencing the stock market should submit detailed sources of wealth and income statements. The measure is expected to apply to brokers, bankers, mutual fund handlers, members of the Capital Market Commission and its subsidiaries.

--The modernisation of the National Greek Tourism Organisation and the exploitation of its assets, as well as the qualitative upgrading of the tourist product, are the major targets for the government's new tourism policy, announced by Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday.

--The breach between industry and commerce is widening as SESME president Costas Veropoulos, representing the commercial sector, said industry was increasingly calling for the state's help and using the pretext that distribution networks were blackmailing them. Federation of Greek Industries president Jason Stratos attempted to cool tempers, saying industry and commerce had to work together as their interests were linked.
--Businesses will be the first to be called on to pay the new real estate tax, following the finance ministry's circular yesterday.
--The Bank of Greece says 1996 saw a veritable explosion in forex lending to private enterprises. The total came to 10.1 billion dollars.

--Calling it the "move of the year", National Bank of Greece officials say the bank is gearing towards a massive share capital increase of 100 billion drachmas that will be directed not only to the domestic but to the international markets. Reports add that the 150-200 million dollar bond loan the bank is to issue on Euro-markets will be ready by May 15.
--The government hopes to save some 200 billion drachmas from servicing the public debt this year due to the gradual redeuction of interest rates.

--Leading entrepreneurs last night sent a message that they were willing to play a leading role in the region as long as they had economic, social and political backing. Intracom's Socrates Kokkalis, DELTA's Dimitris Daskalopoulos and Evangelos Mytilineos of Mytilineos Enterprises were optimistic of success provided there was an improvement in competitiveness and the necessary changes in the job market.

--The Financial Times yesterday noted the significant reduction in the cost of the borrowing in Greece as Reuters Hellas introduces the new Dealing 2000-2 system, both indications that the Greek economy is coming into its own.
--The current accounts deficit rose to 4.5 billion dollars in 1996, over 2.850 in 1995.
